label: BEGINS_2: contingent concrete reality in a history began a finite time ago
definition: BEGINS_2. FiniteDurationBeginningAt h Concrete k v holds when some contingent concrete individual is present at some moment of history v, and every moment at which one is present has a past of finite duration on the clock k (MetricGrimReaper.MetricallyFinitePast: the clock readings of the moments at or before it are bounded below). Read with the physically privileged clock CLOCK_1 (cosmic or proper time). In ordinary language: contingent concrete reality began a finite time ago, whether or not there was a first instant. Examples: discrete or continuous time with a first moment; a populated past that is open below and of finite duration, the order and metric shape of standard FLRW cosmic time (the initial singularity is not a moment). Non-examples: an endless succession of days; any past unbounded below on the clock. Nothing is said about a first moment, an empty moment or a cause.
note: Analyst metric sense of a beginning of the totality of contingent concrete reality; attribution deferred. Relative to the supplied TimeClock and not invariant under reparametrization (CLOCK disambiguation 725f3417-73d0-489f-b8ab-7b2628ff36b7): under ln t an FLRW past is infinite and under arctan an integer past is finite; the intended reading uses CLOCK_1, an OPEN commitment. One clock serves every world of the frame. Strictly weaker than BEGINS_1 in linear time (possiblyFiniteDurationOfFirstMoment; converse fails in MetricBeginningArrival control 2). It is the sense in which the metric Grim Reaper conclusion (PopulatedPastsMetricallyFinite) bears on a beginning.
